name: Kannada
region: Karnataka, in South India, including Bengaluru and Mysuru
about: Kannada is a classical Dravidian language with a written literature going back more than a thousand years, and it has won more Jnanpith awards than almost any other Indian language. Its rounded script is a close cousin of the Telugu script.
pronunciation: Most Kannada words end in a vowel, so say every final u and e clearly, as in hesaru and naale.
Long and short vowels change meaning, so hold the long aa in naanu and the long oo in mooru.
Retroflex sounds like the d in edakke and the l in elu are made with the tongue curled back.
Spoken Kannada often shortens written endings, so chennaagiddene becomes chennaagiddini in everyday talk.

lessons.intro: Namaskaara! Let's begin Kannada with the friendly words you'll hear across Bengaluru, from auto drivers to shopkeepers.
lessons.tip: Kannada uses neevu as the respectful you and for groups, and neenu only with close friends or children. Polite verbs end in i, like kodi and maadi.

phrases.note: Namaskaara is the respectful hello, said with folded hands. It works at any time of day and with anyone.
Hegiddeera is the polite way to ask how are you. People also often ask chennaagiddeera, meaning are you well.
Naanu chennaagiddene means I am fine. In everyday speech you will hear the shorter chennaagiddini.
Dhanyavaadagalu is the full, respectful thank you. In casual city talk, many people simply say thanks in English.
Kshamisi means please forgive me, and works for both sorry and excuse me. In casual speech many people also just say sorry.
Hogi bartini literally means I'll go and come back, the Kannada way of saying goodbye. The host replies hogi banni, go and come back.

lessons.intro: Let's introduce ourselves in Kannada. A little effort goes a long way, and people in Karnataka love hearing visitors try.
lessons.tip: Kannada is a verb final language, so the verb comes at the end, and words like is are often dropped, as in nanna hesaru Priya.

phrases.note: Nanna hesaru Priya means my name is Priya. Hesaru means name, and you just add your own name at the end.
Nimma hesarenu means what is your name. Nimma is the respectful your, so it is safe with anyone.
Neevu elliyavaru means where are you from, literally you are of which place. It is a very common question in Karnataka.
This means I have come from India. Bhaarata is India. A woman can also say naanu Bhaaratadavalu, and a man naanu Bhaaratadavanu.
This means I am happy to have met you. Santosha means happiness, and it is a warm, polite thing to say.
This is how Kannada says I speak a little Kannada, literally a little Kannada comes to me. Swalpa, meaning a little, is a word you'll hear everywhere.

lessons.intro: Let's count in Kannada and talk about time. These are Dravidian numbers, so they will sound quite new compared to Hindi.
lessons.tip: Kannada counting is very regular after ten, so learning one to ten well unlocks the rest. Shops often quote prices in Kannada numbers.

phrases.note: Ondu, eradu, mooru, naalku, aidu. Notice the long oo in mooru, which means three.
Aaru, elu, entu, ombattu, hattu. Seven, elu, has a long e and a curled l sound.
Eega eshtu gante means what time is it now. Gante means hour or o'clock, and many people simply ask time eshtu.
Ivattu is the everyday word for today. In books and news you will also see the formal word indu.
Naale means tomorrow. Say it with a long aa and a clear e at the end.
Ninne means yesterday. Don't mix it up with naale, which is tomorrow.

lessons.intro: Now let's eat and shop in Kannada. From darshinis to street markets, these phrases will help you order and bargain politely.
lessons.tip: Karnataka has a rich vegetarian food culture, from Udupi restaurants to masala dosa and bisi bele bath. Saying you are vegetarian is easy and well understood.

phrases.note: Idara bele eshtu means what is the price of this. In shops people often say just idakke eshtu, how much for this.
Tumba dubaari means very expensive. Follow it with swalpa kammi maadi, please reduce it a little, when bargaining.
Swalpa neeru kodi means please give me some water. Kodi is the polite form of give.
Naanu sasyaahaari means I am vegetarian. In restaurants people also commonly say veg or ask for a veg meal.
Tumba ruchiyaagide means it is very tasty. Ruchi means taste, and this compliment always makes a cook smile.
Bill kodi means please give the bill. Adding the polite kodi keeps it friendly.

lessons.intro: Let's get around in Kannada. Knowing left, right and straight makes every auto ride and walk much easier.
lessons.tip: Polite instructions in Kannada end in i, like tirugi and hogi. Many people mix in English words such as straight and station, which is perfectly normal.

phrases.note: Railu nildaana ellide means where is the railway station. Nildaana is the word on signs, though in speech people often just say railway station ellide.
Edakke tirugi means turn to the left. Eda means left.
Balakke tirugi means turn to the right. Bala means right, and it also means strength.
Neravaagi hogi means go straight. In everyday speech many people just say straight hogi.
Eshtu doora ide means how far is it. Doora means far, and it sounds a lot like Hindi.
Dayavittu sahaaya maadi means please help me. Dayavittu is the word for please, and it makes any request polite.

lessons.intro: Let's finish with words that keep a conversation flowing. These will help you whenever Kannada starts moving a little too fast.
lessons.tip: Kannada speakers often nod with a gentle head wobble while saying haudu. And swalpa adjust maadi, please adjust a little, is a famous Bengaluru phrase.

phrases.note: Haudu means yes and illa means no. Illa also means there isn't, so you will hear it a lot.
Nanage artha aagalilla means I didn't understand, literally the meaning didn't come to me. It is the natural way to ask for help.
This means please speak slowly. Nidhaana means slow, and maataadi is the polite form of speak.
Idara artha enu means what is the meaning of this. Use it for any new word or sign.
Nanage idu ishta aaytu means I liked this. For something you like in general, just say nanage idu ishta.
Shubha raatri means good night. It is a little formal, and among friends many people just say good night in English.
